messages.content:
Outcome: Depression cases (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: no effect
Claim: Genetically determined 25(OH)D was not causally associated with depression in Mendelian randomization analysis.
Sentence: "Although a selection of nine outcomes were reported in previous Mendelian-randomization studies or umbrella reviews to be associated with vitamin D, our MR analysis, with substantial study power (>80% power to detect an association with an odds ratio >1.2 for per standard deviation increase of log-transformed 25[OH]D), was unable to support an interpretation of causal association."
Measured as: depression
Population: 339,256 individuals of White British origin from UK Biobank
Intervention: Genetically determined 25(OH)D level (polygenic risk score, Mendelian randomization)
Comparator: Lower genetically determined 25(OH)D levels
Design: other primary study
Sample size: 339,256
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

## Study B
Found: benefit
Claim: Pregnant women with deficient vitamin D had about twice the odds of a postpartum depression diagnosis compared with those with insufficient or sufficient levels.
Sentence: "In the adjusted model, deficient serum VitD levels were associated with a two-fold-higher likelihood of PPD diagnosis compared to insufficient/sufficient VitD levels (≥20 µg/mL) (OR = 2.0; 95% CI 1.0-4.2; p = 0.049)."
Measured as: postpartum depression diagnosis (M.I.N.I. Plus)
Population: Pregnant women in Pelotas, Brazil, with serum 25(OH)D measured up to 24 weeks of gestation and PPD assessed three months after delivery
Intervention: Gestational vitamin D deficiency (≤19.9 µg/mL), observational exposure
Comparator: Insufficient/sufficient vitamin D (≥20 µg/mL)
Design: cohort study
Sample size: 983
baseline_vitamin_d_status: mixed

content.text: {"rationale":"A well-powered Mendelian randomization null on general depression conflicts with an observational cohort association for postpartum depression, differing in design, population and outcome.","verdict":"genuine","reason":"design_or_bias","also_differs":["population","outcome_measure"],"detail":"MR (n = 339,256, >80% power for OR > 1.2) vs observational cohort (n = 983, OR 2.0, 95% CI 1.0-4.2); postpartum depression in pregnant Brazilian women vs depression in UK Biobank adults"}
